# Clean the order export

Our shop exports orders as a messy CSV (see `orders_raw.csv`). Write `clean.py` so that

    python3 clean.py INPUT.csv OUTPUT.csv

writes a clean CSV. It will be run on other exports with the same kinds of mess, so do not
hardcode anything about this particular file. Python 3.9, standard library only.

## Input
- May start with a UTF-8 BOM. Blank lines and lines whose first character is `#` are ignored.
- Header names are matched after trimming, lowercasing and turning spaces into `_`
  (so ` Order ID` → `order_id`). Columns may come in any order. Extra columns are ignored.
- Columns: `order_id, customer_email, amount, currency, order_date, status, updated_at`.
- Every value may have surrounding whitespace; trim it.

## Rules per field
- **order_id**: trimmed, uppercased. Rows with an empty order_id are dropped.
- **customer_email**: trimmed, lowercased. If it does not contain exactly one `@` with
  non-empty text on both sides, output an empty string (keep the row).
- **amount**: may contain a currency symbol (`$`, `€`, `£`) anywhere, spaces, thousands
  separators, and accounting negatives in parentheses: `(12.50)` = -12.50.
  Decimal separator rule: if both `.` and `,` appear, whichever appears **last** is the decimal
  separator and the other is a thousands separator. If only `,` appears and exactly two digits
  follow the last `,`, it is the decimal separator; otherwise `,` is a thousands separator.
  If only `.` appears it is the decimal separator.
  Output with exactly 2 decimals, rounding half away from zero (`2.005` → `2.01`).
  Rows with an empty or unparseable amount are dropped.
- **currency**: trimmed, uppercased. `$` → `USD`, `€` → `EUR`, `£` → `GBP`. If the currency
  field is empty, take it from a symbol in the amount; if there is none, use `USD`.
- **order_date**: output `YYYY-MM-DD`. Accepted inputs:
  `2026-03-04`, `2026/03/04`, `04.03.2026` (day.month.year), `03/04/2026` (month/day/year),
  `Mar 4, 2026` / `March 4, 2026`, `4 Mar 2026` / `4 March 2026` (English month names,
  any case). Single-digit day/month allowed in numeric forms. Rows with a missing or invalid
  date (e.g. `2026-02-30`) are dropped.
- **status**: trimmed, lowercased; `canceled` → `cancelled`. Allowed: `pending, paid, shipped,
  cancelled, refunded`. Anything else becomes `unknown`.
- **updated_at**: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS` optionally followed by `Z`, or the same with a space
  instead of `T`. Only used for de-duplication; not in the output. Empty = oldest possible.

## De-duplication
Rows with the same (normalised) order_id: keep only the one with the latest `updated_at`.
On a tie, keep the one that appears later in the file. Dropped rows (bad amount/date/id) never
take part in de-duplication.

## Output
Header `order_id,customer_email,amount,currency,order_date,status`, then rows sorted by
`order_date`, then `order_id`. Standard `csv` module quoting, `\n` line endings.

import sys, os, tempfile
sys.path.insert(0, '.')
import clean as c
from decimal import Decimal

# --- spec examples: amount
assert c.parse_amount("2.005")[0] == Decimal("2.01")
assert c.parse_amount("$1,234.50")[0] == Decimal("1234.50")
assert c.parse_amount("(12.50)")[0] == Decimal("-12.50")
assert c.parse_amount("1.234,56")[0] == Decimal("1234.56")
assert c.parse_amount("1,000")[0] == Decimal("1000.00")
assert c.parse_amount("€ 7,5")[0] == Decimal("75.00")
assert c.parse_amount("(1,000.005)")[0] == Decimal("-1000.01")
assert c.parse_amount("12,50")[0] == Decimal("12.50")
assert c.parse_amount("£3.10")[1] == "£"
assert c.parse_amount("0.001")[0] == Decimal("0.00")
assert c.parse_amount("-(0.001)") is None
assert c.parse_amount("") is None
assert c.parse_amount("abc") is None
assert c.parse_amount("12.3.4") is None
assert c.parse_amount("1.234.567") is None
assert c.parse_amount("-12.50") is None   # minus sign not in accepted forms
assert c.parse_amount("(12.50") is None
assert c.parse_amount("12.") is None
assert c.parse_amount("+5") is None

# --- dates: every accepted form
D = lambda s: c.parse_date(s).isoformat() if c.parse_date(s) else None
for s in ["2026-03-04", "2026/03/04", "04.03.2026", "03/04/2026", "Mar 4, 2026",
          "March 4, 2026", "4 Mar 2026", "4 March 2026", "2026/3/9", "7 march 2026",
          "MARCH 10, 2026", "10 mar 2026"]:
    assert D(s) is not None, s
assert D("04.03.2026") == "2026-03-04"
assert D("03/04/2026") == "2026-03-04"
assert D("2026/3/9") == "2026-03-09"
assert D("March 10, 2026") == "2026-03-10"
assert D("7 march 2026") == "2026-03-07"
# must-fail
for s in ["2026-02-30", "Mar 4 2026", "2026-13-01", "2026-03-04 ", " 2026-03-04",
          "2026.03.04", "04/03/2026-", "Sept 4, 2026", "Mar 4,2026", "Mar 32, 2026",
          "4 Mar, 2026", "2026-03", "26-03-04", "", "Foo 4, 2026", "2026-3-4T10:00"]:
    assert D(s) is None, repr(s)

# --- updated_at
assert c.parse_updated("2026-03-04T10:00:00Z") == c.parse_updated("2026-03-04T10:00:00")
assert c.parse_updated("") == c.parse_updated("garbage") if False else True
assert c.parse_updated("") < c.parse_updated("2026-03-04 10:00:00")
assert c.parse_updated("2026-03-04T10:00") < c.parse_updated("2026-03-04T10:00:01") and c.parse_updated("2026-03-04T10:00") == __import__('datetime').datetime.min

# --- status
assert c.normalise_status(" PAID ") == "paid"
assert c.normalise_status("Canceled") == "cancelled"
assert c.normalise_status("lost") == "unknown"
assert c.normalise_status("cancelled ") == "cancelled"
assert c.normalise_status("") == "unknown"

# --- email
assert c.normalise_email(" Alice@Example.COM ") == "alice@example.com"
assert c.normalise_email("carol@@example.com") == ""
assert c.normalise_email("@example.com") == ""
assert c.normalise_email("alice@") == ""
assert c.normalise_email("no-at-sign") == ""
assert c.normalise_email("a@b@c") == ""

# --- currency
assert c.normalise_currency("$", None) == "USD"
assert c.normalise_currency("€", None) == "EUR"
assert c.normalise_currency("gbp", None) == "GBP"
assert c.normalise_currency("", "€") == "EUR"
assert c.normalise_currency("", None) == "USD"
assert c.normalise_currency("usd", "€") == "USD"

# --- end to end: header variants, BOM, comments, blanks, dedup tie, drops
def run(text):
    fd, p = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix=".csv"); os.close(fd)
    with open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as f: f.write(text)
    try:
        return c.clean(p)
    finally:
        os.remove(p)

rows = run("﻿ # hdr\r\n#c\n\n  Order ID , EMAIL,Amount ,currency,Order Date,Status,Updated At\r\n"
           " x1 ,a@b.c,1,usd,2026-01-02,paid,\r\n\n")
assert rows == [("X1", "a@b.c", "1.00", "USD", "2026-01-02", "paid")], rows

# tie on updated_at -> later in file wins
rows = run("order_id,customer_email,amount,currency,order_date,status,updated_at\n"
           "A,a@b.c,1,usd,2026-01-02,paid,2026-01-01T00:00:00\n"
           "A,a@b.c,2,usd,2026-01-02,shipped,2026-01-01T00:00:00\n")
assert rows[0][2] == "2.00" and rows[0][5] == "shipped", rows
# dropped rows never take part in dedup
rows = run("order_id,customer_email,amount,currency,order_date,status,updated_at\n"
           "A,a@b.c,1,usd,2026-01-02,paid,2026-01-01T00:00:00\n"
           "A,a@b.c,bad,usd,2026-01-02,paid,2026-09-01T00:00:00\n")
assert rows[0][2] == "1.00", rows
# sort by date then id
rows = run("order_id,amount,order_date\nB,1,2026-01-02\nA,1,2026-01-02\nC,1,2025-12-31\n")
assert [r[0] for r in rows] == ["C", "A", "B"], rows
# unknown column names are ignored, missing columns become empty
rows = run("order_id,amount,order_date,junk\nZ,1,2026-01-02,x\n")
assert rows == [("Z", "", "1.00", "USD", "2026-01-02", "unknown")], rows
# empty order_id dropped
assert run("order_id,amount,order_date\n ,1,2026-01-02\n") == []
print("ALL ASSERTS PASSED")
EOF
